title: Polynomial-time transducer semantics
statement: Let $S$ be a finite state set with decidable equality, let $\delta:S\times\{0,1\}\to S$ be a transition function, let $\varepsilon:S\times\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}\cup\{\text{no output}\}$ be a per-bit emission rule, let $\phi:S\to\{0,1\}\cup\{\text{no output}\}$ be a final emission rule, and choose a start state $q_0\in S$. The word function that emits according to $\varepsilon$ on each input bit, updates its state by $\delta$, and emits according to $\phi$ at the end is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: The state set has decidable equality
A transition function on states and bits
replaced:
For every finite state set with transition, per-bit emission, final emission, and
start state, the associated word-transducer function on binary strings is
polynomial-time computable, with the exact time bound $n + 1$.
